st: Peel the potatoes and grate them on the fine side of a grater, along with the onion.
Squeeze the grated potato in a clean towel to remove as much liquid as possible. Pour off the liquid but keep the starch at the bottom.
Mix the potato with the egg, [[3 tbsp]] flour, [[1 tsp]] salt, pepper and the saved starch.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Spoon in portions of batter and flatten each to about 1/2 inch thick.
Fry 4 to 5 minutes per side until deep golden and crisp, adding oil as needed.
Drain the pancakes on paper towels.
Serve hot with [[0.5 cup]] sour cream.
Brown the pork in [[1 tbsp]] butter over medium-high heat for 8 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Add the onions and cook 6 minutes until soft and golden.
Pour in [[2 cups]] broth, add the bay leaves, cover, and simmer 40 minutes until the pork is tender.
Add the sausage and cook 8 minutes.
Melt [[2 tbsp]] butter in a small pan, whisk in [[3 tbsp]] flour, and cook 2 minutes until pale gold.
Whisk a ladle of hot liquid into the roux, then stir it into the stew to thicken.
Stir in [[0.75 cup]] sour cream and heat gently for 3 minutes without boiling.
Serve hot with draniki or bread for dipping.
Mix [[3 cups]] flour, the egg and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Add about [[0.5 cup]] warm water to form a firm dough.
Knead 8 minutes, wrap, and rest 30 minutes.
Cook the pork and onion in [[1 tbsp]] butter for 8 minutes until the pork reaches 160°F (71°C).
Mix in the mashed potato, [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper. Cool the filling.
Roll the dough thin and cut into 3-inch circles.
Put a spoonful of filling on each and fold into half-moons, pressing the edges firmly closed.
Boil the dumplings in salted water for 6 to 7 minutes until they float and the dough is tender.
Drain, toss with [[1 tbsp]] butter and serve with [[0.5 cup]] sour cream.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and butter a 9x13-inch dish.
Cook the bacon in a skillet for 7 minutes until crisp, keeping the fat in the pan.
Grate the potatoes finely and drain them in a towel. Mix with the grated onion.
Add the eggs, [[0.5 cup]] sour cream, [[2 tbsp]] flour, [[1.5 tsp]] salt and pepper.
Stir in the bacon and 2 tablespoons of the bacon fat.
Spread in the dish and level the top.
Bake 60 to 70 minutes until the top is deep golden and the center is cooked through.
Rest 10 minutes, cut into squares, and serve with more sour cream.
Boil the beets in water for 40 minutes until a knife slides in easily, then cool, peel and grate or dice them.
Boil and peel the eggs if not already done.
Mix the beets with [[4 cups]] kefir and [[1 cup]] cold water in a large bowl.
Stir in the cucumber, dill, green onions and optional radishes.
Season with [[1 tsp]] salt and [[1 tbsp]] lemon juice.
Chill at least 1 hour until very cold. The soup will turn bright pink.
Serve in bowls topped with chopped eggs and extra dill.
Put the beef and [[10 cups]] water in a large pot. Bring to a boil, skim foam, then simmer 60 minutes until tender.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a skillet and cook the onion and carrots 5 minutes.
Add the beets, [[2 tbsp]] tomato paste and [[1 tbsp]] vinegar and cook 8 minutes. The vinegar helps keep the beets red.
Add the potatoes and bay leaf to the broth and simmer 10 minutes.
Add the cabbage and simmer 10 minutes.
Stir in the beet mixture and garlic and simmer 10 minutes.
Season with [[2 tsp]] salt, remove the bay leaf, and rest 10 minutes.
Serve with [[0.5 cup]] sour cream and dill.
Mix [[1.5 cups]] flour, the eggs, mashed potato and [[0.5 tsp]] salt into a soft, thick batter, adding a splash of milk if too stiff.
Cook the onion in [[2 tbsp]] butter for 6 minutes until golden.
Bring [[4 cups]] water with [[0.5 tsp]] salt to a gentle boil.
Drop in spoonfuls of batter, using a wet spoon, and cook 5 to 6 minutes until they float and are firm.
Lift the dumplings out with a slotted spoon.
Heat [[3 cups]] milk gently and add the dumplings. Do not boil.
Add the onion and butter, sprinkle with dill, and serve warm.

ing: farmer's cheese or dry cottage cheese, drained well
st: Drain the cheese in a fine sieve for 10 minutes and press out extra liquid.
Mash the cheese with the egg, [[2 tbsp]] sugar, [[1 tsp]] vanilla and a pinch of salt.
Stir in [[0.5 cup]] flour until a soft, slightly sticky dough forms.
With floured hands, shape into 8 patties about 1/2 inch thick.
Dust each lightly in flour.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] oil in a skillet over medium-low heat.
Fry 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden brown, flipping gently.
Serve warm with [[0.5 cup]] sour cream, jam or honey.
